strings.d1.s0.name: Museo del Prado
strings.d1.s0.tips: Velázquez's Las Meninas, Goya, Bosch. Book a timed slot online (15 EUR); entry is free 18:00-20:00 but crowded.
strings.d1.s1.name: Parque del Retiro
strings.d1.s1.tips: The lake (rowing boats 6 EUR), the Crystal Palace and the Fallen Angel statue.
strings.d1.s2.name: Casa Alberto
strings.d1.s2.tips: A tavern dating from 1827 in Huertas; try the rabo de toro (oxtail stew) and vermouth.
strings.d1.s3.name: Museo Reina Sofía
strings.d1.s3.tips: Picasso's Guernica; free on Saturdays after 14:30.
strings.d1.s4.name: Barrio de las Letras
strings.d1.s4.tips: Cervantes' neighbourhood, with verses written in the streets and Plaza Santa Ana.
strings.d1.b0.name: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza
strings.d1.b0.tips: The third museum of the Golden Triangle of Art; an alternative to the Reina Sofía.
strings.d1.b1.name: Mercado de San Miguel
strings.d1.b1.tips: Tapas stalls in an iron-framed market hall; touristy but worth seeing.
strings.d2.theme: Habsburg Madrid and the Royal Palace
strings.d2.s0.name: Plaza Mayor
strings.d2.s0.tips: The square is empty in the morning; try a bocadillo de calamares (fried squid sandwich) at Casa Rúa.
strings.d2.s1.name: Royal Palace of Madrid
strings.d2.s1.tips: Western Europe's largest palace; book a timed slot online. See the Throne Room and the Sabatini Gardens.
strings.d2.s2.name: Almudena Cathedral
strings.d2.s2.tips: Opposite the palace; look up at the colourful ceiling.
strings.d2.s3.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
strings.d2.s3.tips: Churros con chocolate served around the clock since 1894.
strings.d2.s4.name: La Latina Cava Baja Tapas
strings.d2.s4.tips: A tapas crawl along Cava Baja: Casa Lucio (huevos rotos), Juana la Loca (tortilla), Txirimiri.
strings.d2.b0.name: Casa Botín
strings.d2.b0.tips: The world's oldest restaurant (1725); order the cochinillo (roast suckling pig) and reserve ahead.
strings.d2.b1.name: Temple of Debod
strings.d2.b1.tips: An Egyptian temple, famous for its sunset; an alternative to the cathedral.
strings.d3.s0.name: Gran Vía
strings.d3.s0.tips: Madrid's Broadway, with the Metropolis Building and the Schweppes sign.
strings.d3.s1.name: Malasaña Streets
strings.d3.s1.tips: Vintage and record shops, plus Plaza del Dos de Mayo.
strings.d3.s2.name: Mercado de San Ildefonso
strings.d3.s2.tips: A street-food market on Calle Fuencarral.
strings.d3.s3.name: Chueca
strings.d3.s3.tips: A colourful neighbourhood; head up to the rooftop bar at Mercado de San Antón.
strings.d3.s4.name: Círculo de Bellas Artes Terrace
strings.d3.s4.tips: A rooftop terrace above Gran Vía, with sunset views and Calle de Alcalá below.
strings.d3.b0.name: Lamiak Malasaña
strings.d3.b1.name: Museo de Historia de Madrid
strings.d3.b1.tips: The city history museum in Malasaña; free entry.
strings.d4.s0.name: Toledo Cathedral
strings.d4.s0.tips: AVE train from Atocha, 33 minutes. Spain's largest Gothic cathedral, with works by El Greco.
strings.d4.s1.name: Iglesia de Santo Tomé
strings.d4.s1.tips: El Greco's The Burial of the Count of Orgaz.
strings.d4.s2.name: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
strings.d4.s2.tips: A Mudéjar synagogue in the Jewish quarter.
strings.d4.s3.name: Cervecería El Trébol
strings.d4.s3.tips: Bombas (stuffed potato croquettes) and carcamusas (pork and tomato stew) in Toledo; a local favourite.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mirador del Valle
strings.d4.s4.tips: The Toledo skyline seen across the river. Take the tourist bus or a taxi, and head back by 17:00.
strings.d4.b0.name: Alcázar of Toledo
strings.d4.b0.tips: An army museum with city views; an alternative to the mirador.
strings.d4.b1.name: Mazapán Santo Tomé
strings.d5.s0.name: Aqueduct of Segovia
strings.d5.s0.tips: AVE train, 27 minutes. A 2,000-year-old Roman aqueduct built without mortar, 28 m high.
strings.d5.s1.name: Segovia Cathedral
strings.d5.s1.tips: The last Gothic cathedral built in Spain, on Plaza Mayor.
strings.d5.s2.name: Alcázar of Segovia
strings.d5.s2.tips: Said to have inspired Disney's castle; the tower has 152 steps.
strings.d5.s3.name: Mesón de Cándido
strings.d5.s3.tips: Cochinillo (suckling pig) beneath the aqueduct since 1898, carved at the table with a plate.
strings.d5.s4.name: Mirador de la Pradera de San Marcos
strings.d5.s4.tips: The view of the Alcázar like a ship's prow, from the riverside.
strings.d5.b0.name: José María Segovia
strings.d5.b1.name: Royal Palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso
strings.d5.b1.tips: A Versailles-style palace 11 km from Segovia; an alternative to the mirador.
strings.d6.s0.name: Museo Sorolla
strings.d6.s0.tips: The painter's home, with an Andalusian-style garden; quiet in the morning.
strings.d6.s1.name: Barrio de Salamanca Calle Serrano
strings.d6.s1.tips: A luxury shopping street, near the Platea gastro-theatre.
strings.d6.s2.name: Platea Madrid
strings.d6.s2.tips: A food market in a former cinema, near Colón.
strings.d6.s3.name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium Tour
strings.d6.s3.tips: Real Madrid museum and stadium tour; go when there is no match.
strings.d6.s4.name: National Archaeological Museum
strings.d6.s4.tips: Home of the Lady of Elche, in Salamanca district; a good escape from the heat.
strings.d6.b0.name: Lhardy
strings.d6.b0.tips: A restaurant dating from 1839; try the cocido madrileño (Madrid chickpea stew), served Monday to Wednesday.
strings.d6.b1.name: Parque de El Capricho
strings.d6.b1.tips: A romantic park, open at weekends; an alternative to the stadium.
strings.d7.theme: Rastro and Lavapiés: a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: El Rastro
strings.d7.s0.tips: A huge flea market on Sundays (Ribera de Curtidores); on other days, antique shops.
strings.d7.s1.name: Lavapiés
strings.d7.s1.tips: A multicultural neighbourhood with murals and the Tabacalera arts centre.
strings.d7.s2.name: Casa Revuelta
strings.d7.s2.tips: A tapa of bacalao rebozado (battered cod), eaten standing up near El Rastro; open since 1966.
strings.d7.s3.name: Puerta del Sol Kilometre Zero
strings.d7.s3.tips: Spain's zero point and the Bear statue. Take the metro to Atocha; the airport is 30 minutes by Cercanías.
strings.d7.b0.name: Taberna La Concha La Latina
strings.d7.b1.name: Museo Cerralbo
strings.d7.b1.tips: An aristocratic mansion; an alternative to Lavapiés.
strings.note0: A 10-trip metro ticket costs 12.20 EUR; the airport is 30 minutes by metro or Cercanías. Toledo and Segovia are 30 minutes by AVE (Atocha/Chamartín); buy tickets in advance.
strings.note1: The Prado, the Palace and the Reina Sofía require timed online tickets. The Prado is free 18:00-20:00 and the Reina Sofía on Saturday afternoons (expect queues).
strings.note2: Winter is sunny at 5-12°C. In December there is a Christmas market on Plaza Mayor; January brings the sales and it is cocido season.
strings.note3: Tapas cost 2-4 EUR, a menú del día 13-16 EUR and cochinillo 30-40 EUR; churros at San Ginés cost 5 EUR. Round up the bill as a tip.
strings.note4: Visit El Rastro on a Sunday morning; Lavapiés and Malasaña are best in the evening. Watch for pickpockets around Sol and on the metro.
strings.note5: If Real Madrid are playing, buy tickets months ahead; stadium tours run daily.
